guard.refuse_dropped_advice: ledger not written. Either prepare the input, or pass --allow-drop explicitly (and record the dropped keys in HISTORY).
guard.refuse_changed: this re-measure would **change %(count)d fact values** (unaccepted changes):
guard.accepted_boundary: accepted %(accepted)d via --accept-changes: %(keys)s — the rest still refused.
guard.refuse_changed_advice: ledger not written. Confirm each change is **measured, not guessed** (not missing input / not a broken instrument), then pass --accept-changes (or --accept-changes=k1,k2 per key).
guard.empty_ledger: no facts measured at all. An empty ledger is not a pass (zero-value guard).
guard.write_target_gitignored: ledger target %(path)s is covered by .gitignore — writing there is writing nowhere (version control cannot see it; the hooks read a different ledger); drop that ignore rule, or set REFLECT_FACTS to a tracked location
guard.write_target_no_git: (not a git repo or git unavailable: skipping the gitignore check)
guard.write_target_env_carrier: this repo has Einfacht.env but this process did not load it (REFLECT_FACTS used the code default) — source it first when running by hand, otherwise the write target may differ from the hooks' context (issue #20 ②)
guard.write_target_env_carrier_after: %(prefix)s; this repo has Einfacht.env but this process did not load it (REFLECT_FACTS used the code default) — source it first when running by hand, otherwise the write target may differ from the hooks' context (issue #20 ②)
guard.module_banner: guard is a module (called by facts.measure); it does not run standalone. --selftest shows its selftest.
